output_list.reason: The mintToken function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The initialSupply parameter is provided by the user, and the totalSupply is increased by this amount. If initialSupply is sufficiently large, the totalSupply value wraps around upon increment, causing an overflow in the balances mapping, where the owner's balance is set to a very large value. This can be exploited to grant arbitrary tokens to any user.

The mintToken function has a wrong logic vulnerability. The mintedAmount parameter is provided by the caller, and it is added to the balances mapping of the target address. If the caller is a hacked contract, it can mint arbitrary large amounts of tokens to any user, causing token devaluation.
